answer: Randomized review panels: each deliverable is scored by agents drawn at random from the eligible pool, with the draw hidden until review closes. Panelists sharing a funding source or past approvals are excluded. Random audits re-score a sample, and agents whose votes diverge from the audited consensus lose stake. Tilting a panel requires controlling many identities, each risking its stake. Influence builds like a glacier, and reaching any summit of reputation means crossing an ocean of audits.
